dimensions.explanation: The strongest reading covers a specific product or a particular product type, including linked fund types or fund houses, when a distributor promotes to a client. A narrower named-product-only reading is possible only by disregarding the express product-type language.

A guaranteed return is typically composed of the underlying fund return and a distributor top-up. The source does not itself classify every component as a gift; gift and discount status require offer-specific judgment.
The fee or charge discount exception attaches to the gift prohibition. It does not, on the supplied text, immunise a distinct non-discount gift or top-up bundled with a discount.
The operative rule is ‘should not offer’; the circular separately says returns or incentives may be considered gifts. This is a conduct restriction, not the section 103 offence.
The control applies when the distributor promotes the product or product type to a client. No commencement, deadline, or transition rule is supplied.
The FAQ answer referenced by footnote 3 and the complete Code provisions remain necessary to resolve classification boundaries; section 103 and advertising rules are separate dependencies.

readings.distinction: The exception is component-specific: a fee or charge discount is excluded from the gift prohibition, while a distinct non-discount gift remains caught. Product-type promotion is expressly included. A guaranteed return is not automatically a gift; classification is required.

assumptions: The offer is assessed as one indivisible package.
The package is treated according to its dominant or principal economic character, if such a character can be established.

readings.distinction: A competing reading treats the exception as applying to the combined package when its principal character is a fee or charge discount. The supplied text does not provide a dominance or inseparability test, so this reading is materially less supported and cannot be operationalised without additional authority.
